smbd_deltas: the two rips agree cell for cell from column 0 to column 49 and then part company. followed here, all from the smbd challenge rip: (1) the four-column tree at 50-53 has its canopy on row 10, three rows higher than the nes map's row 13. (2) every platform from the lift pit on is two columns left of its nes column - the trees at 96-99, 102-109, 111-113, 114-117 and 120-123 are the nes map's 98-101, 104-111, 113-115, 116-119 and 122-125, and the coin runs over them move with them. (3) the nes map has a fourth lift deck over the closing ground at 131-133 on row 6; smbd has open sky and two clouds there instead. (4) the closing ground starts at 128 instead of 129. (5) the staircase is six columns and seven blocks tall at 136-141 where the nes map's is six columns and eight blocks tall at 138-143, and the flagpole stands eight columns past its last column (149) instead of nine (152) - the same eight-past spacing 1-1 and 1-2 measured. (6) the castle keep moves with it, tower at 155-157 instead of 158-160. challenge mode's own additions - five red coins and the yoshi egg above - are recorded in "smbd" and are not compiled.
confidence_notes: 1-3 is transcribed cell by cell from the two map rips above, the way 1-1 and 1-2 were: every 16x16 cell of both images was hashed and classified against a tile sheet cut from the same image (37 distinct tiles in the nes rip, 59 in the smbd one), the two classifications were diffed column by column, and the smbd geometry was followed wherever they differ (see smbd_deltas). the nes rip is 176 columns of content and 15 rows, aligned to the grid this schema uses with no offset - image row 13 is the ground surface. the smbd rip is 160 columns and is cropped to rows 2-13 (8 px down from a row boundary), so rows 0-1 and row 14 were read off the nes rip, where they hold nothing but sky and the bottom of the trunks. what stays approx: the start column (no rip draws mario), and every lift's travel, because a map rip catches a moving deck at one instant - the decks' rows and their drawn columns are measured, the spans they run are the pits they have to bridge. the 23 coins are the smbd rip's 21 plus the two cells challenge mode reddens inside a coin run (28,4 and 112,12), which is exactly the nes rip's 23 coins at the smbd columns. two clouds (35,7 and 96,10) are drawn behind a canopy in both rips and so cannot land at all under the compiler's whole-shape scenery rule. the level has no hills and no bushes: over open air there is no ground for either to stand on, and neither rip draws one. themushroomkingdom.net and vgmaps.de were cited by the earlier prose pass and carried no coordinates, so they are no longer listed as sources; the mariowiki page is kept for the non-positional facts it supplied (the coin total, the power-up's contents, the medal scores) and every coordinate here comes from the two rips.
